title: DuckDuckGo for iOS
description: Build a SwiftUI/WebKit browser sample with search routing, tabs, settings, tracker-rule demonstrations, and a private-mode data policy.
problem: Learners need a source-grounded way to understand and extend DuckDuckGo for iOS while separating implemented behavior from demo data, simulations, and missing integrations.
audience: Third-year undergraduate students who have completed introductory programming and want a practical mobile mini-project.
prerequisites: Git basics and ability to run the platform tooling described in the source README
learning_outcomes: Explain and trace input classification, scheme handling, empty input, and search-engine selection in its named source files.
Explain and trace browsertab identity, selected-tab behavior, close rules, and userdefaults persistence in its named source files.
Explain and trace uiviewrepresentable/webkit bridge, navigation state, and page loading in its named source files.
Explain and trace rule-list json, rule compilation, blocked-count reporting, and private data behavior in its named source files.
Explain and trace observable store injection, navigation, toolbar actions, and settings binding in its named source files.
Explain and trace xctest coverage, xcodegen project configuration, and documentation boundary in its named source files.
Distinguish unit-test evidence from device, service, and deployment evidence.
Propose a safe, bounded extension without describing it as already implemented.
